newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho opposition calls on King to dissolve govt.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho opposition calls on King to dissolve govt.

text.p: Supporters of five Lesotho opposition parties marched to the royal palace in Maseru on Wednesday in defiance of a recent protest ban imposed by Prime Minister Ntsu Mokhehle.
The march was the third in two weeks led by opposition party leaders unhappy with the Mokhehle government.

In a petition presented to Lesotho's King Letsie III through his senior private secretary, the parties said that since Mokhehle had established the new Lesotho Congress for Democracy he had continued to govern the country illegally.
The petition called on King Letsie to dissolve the government and establish an interim government to prepare for democratic elections before peace was destroyed in the tiny kingdom.
The opposition supporters said divisions in the government had further split the people of Lesotho.

Mokhehle resigned from the Basotholand Congress Party last month after 45 years as leader and formed the Lesotho Congress for Democracy after it became clear that he might not be re-elected as party chief at a congress set for July.
His entire government and 44 of the 64 BCP members in the 65-seat parliament backed his move, but 20 legislators refused to accept it and continue to threaten legal action.

Asked about the recent ban on marches, the leader of the opposition Marematlou Freedom Party, Vincent Malebo, said: "Nobody can stop us from going to the palace because it is our traditional and constitutional right to do so."
Deputy Prime Minister Pakalitha Mosisili announced the ban on marches to the royal palace and said any grievances should be channelled through the ministry responsible.
